content:
The test image shows a green plant stem with abundant white, cottony/fluffy mycelial growth spreading outward from it onto the surrounding surface. This is classic fungal mycelium on a stem.

Top candidates:
- **Sclerotinia_Timber_Rot**: produces dense white cottony mycelium on stems
- **Gray_Mold**: produces grayish fuzzy growth (Botrytis)
- **Rhizopus_Soft_Rots**: white cottony growth but typically on fruit

The very white, dense, spreading mycelium on a stem strongly points to Sclerotinia. Let me confirm with one reference image.

The reference shows Sclerotinia sclerotia (dark hardened bodies), while the test image shows the mycelial stage — dense white cottony growth spreading from a stem. This mycelial pattern is still characteristic of Sclerotinia_Timber_Rot (the pathogen produces abundant white mycelium on stems before forming sclerotia). The Bugwood image ID 1572831 in the test image is also from the Bugwood database, consistent with this disease category.

The dense white mycelial mat radiating from the stem tissue is classic Sclerotinia timber rot.
